thread:
alice: Heads-up — running prod-like load against awq-int8 + prefix-cache and seeing weird latency oscillations and tail spikes (~200ms -> 800ms) when continuous-batching is enabled. Not repro with fp8 profile.

ben: Hmm that sounds like cache thrash. Are you using per-request keying or global prefix keys?

alice: Per-customer prefix keys (hashed request prefix). We suspect KV cache churn because AWQ has slightly different tokenization and smaller KV density after quant, causing larger mem working set.

carol: Could be batching interaction too — continuous batching holds the request open while waiting for batcher timeout; if cache miss rate increases the backend fetches kvs more often -> higher p99. Did you check batch sizes/timings?

alice: Yes, here's the test config we used:

```
model_profile: awq-int8-v2
deployment: dedicated-staging
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_wait_ms: 12
  max_batch: 64
prefix_cache:
  enabled: true
  key_mode: customer_hash
  ttl_ms: 300000
```

dave: What about accuracy deltas during quant? If AWQ is producing different tokenization / outputs, cache hits might be logically invalid (same prefix -> different next tokens). That could cause our reranking/metrics to mismatch. Any eval diffs?

alice: Good point — we ran the regression harness on the same seed prompt set. AWQ-int8 raw BLEU/qa-f1 summary: -0.8% relative vs fp16 baseline on long-context set, but perplexity delta modest. FP8 had +0.1% (basically flat).

ben: So quality delta isn't catastrophic but not zero. That may invalidate cached prefixes if the cached response was generated under fp16 semantics. We need prefix cache tagging by quant-profile + tokenizer-hash. Quick fix: include model_quant_tag in cache key.

carol: Agree. Also consider adding a small jitter to batching release to avoid synchronized bursts when cache miss spike happens. For example: max_wait_ms: 12 -> random(8..14).

alice: Trying two experiments: (A) cache-key = prefix+quant_tag, batching max_wait_ms=12 fixed; (B) cache-key=prefix only, batching jitter enabled. Will run 6-hour soak with synthetic QPS=1200.

ci-bot: CI:perf-suite started run 1790123501 on awq-int8-v2 with tag quant-cache-key-sweep. Results will post in thread when done.

ben: Also instrument these metrics: cache_hit_rate by quant_tag, p99 latency by batch_size, kv_fetches/sec, downstream model drops. If you can capture tokenization-hash collisions that'll help.

alice: Test A finished: cache hit rate by quant_tag enabled -> hit_rate 78% (was 65), p99 dropped from 780ms -> 210ms, throughput steady. Accuracy regression unchanged (-0.82%).

alice: Test B finished: jitter batching -> hit_rate 66% (no change), p99 460ms (improvement but still noisy), throughput variance lower.

dave: Conclusion: keying cache by quant profile is the low-effort correct fix. For long-term, we should surface model-compatibility flags in model catalog (can this share prefix caches with other quantized variants?).

carol: I'll open infra task to add quant_tag to cache key and add batching jitter flag defaulted off for older deployments. Also add telemetry dashboard for cache-hit-by-model-variant.

ben: One more note: for FP8 we didn't see the same mem expansion — curious if kernel layout differs. Might be worth a small profiling job on kv memory footprint for awq vs fp8.

alice: Filing followups: 1) infra task for cache-key change (#7712), 2) perf job to profile kv mem per quant variant (#7713), 3) docs update for model-catalog compatibility. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
